title: The optimal Hessian bound for convex four-body central configurations
abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 7.3 of arXiv:2609.35632 on the central configurations of the planar Newtonian four-body problem. At every strictly convex central configuration of four positive masses, the Hessian form Q of U + (λ/2)I is at least two thirds of its radial part K, and strictly so wherever K is positive. In the notation of the paper this is λ_max(G) < 1/3 for the explicit 2×2 matrix G of its Proposition 3.5, and by its Proposition 7.2 the constant 2/3 is optimal. It sharpens Theorem B of the paper, Q ≥ K/4. The definitions and the reduction to the normal form of Corbera, Cors and Roberts are those of the registered development lean4body-uniqueness. The new parts are a majorant that pays only the largest eigenvalue of S(y), an exact test that is positive definite exactly when λ_max(G) < 1/3, and a computer-assisted proof of that test: a branch and bound with interval arithmetic over the three-dimensional set of normalized convex central configurations, reduced by a symmetry to half of it, and an exact Taylor-form theorem at the corner where the margin of the test vanishes. Lean's kernel checks the certificates with `decide +kernel`. The trusted base is Lean's kernel, including its built-in arithmetic on natural-number literals (GMP-accelerated), and the proofs use only Lean's three standard axioms.
